chunks: He made them, in that regard, the trustees of His revelation, and entrusted them with the deposits of His command and prohibition to the Messengers,
and He protected them from the doubt of uncertainties, so none of them deviates from the path of His pleasure.
and He reinforced them with the benefits of assistance, and ignited in their hearts the humility of the tranquility of submission.
and He opened for them easy doors to His Glories, and set up for them a clear beacon upon the signs of His Oneness.
The burdens of sins did not weigh them down, nor did the heels of nights and days make them move (from their station).
And doubts did not strike with their arrows the firmness of their faith, nor did misgivings assault the bases of their certainty.
And the spark of malice did not ignite among them, nor did bewilderment deprive them of what they encountered of His knowledge in their inner selves.
And from His greatness and awe of His majesty settled within their bosoms, and evil thoughts did not covet them to cast their lot upon their minds.

key_terms.تَوَاضُعَ إِخْبَاتِ ٱلسَّكِينَةِ: Humility of the tranquility of submission

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual characteristics and divine protections of the Imams according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In the context of the 'Al-Ashbaah' chapter, this passage articulates the doctrine of Ismah (infallibility) and 'Ismah al-A'yan (protection from error), positioning the Ahl al-Bayt as the divine trustees (Dawa'i) who preserve the essence of revelation. It underscores their psychological and spiritual immunity from Shubuhat (doubts) and Waswas (whispers), establishing them as the manifest signs (Manar) of Tawhid and the perfect exemplars of human tranquility (Sakinah) in Shia theology.
